solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inexpensive carpet only initially has pile

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word carpet is wanted here

parts.note: a pile is a heap

explanation.surface: A cheap rug that has a deep pile only when first bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only initially' takes C, the first letter of 'carpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something low in price.

clue.text: Clubs request a lot of beer?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A golf club asking for a large order of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel holds a large quantity of beer; the question mark flags the definition by description.

clue.text: Gem's not the first for noble

indicators.note: the opening letter of the gem's name is dropped

parts.note: a pearl is a gem

explanation.surface: A jewel that is not the finest, given to an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the P from PEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the British nobility, ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Bit some food, bit by bit

parts.note: a bit is a piece
a meal is a serving of food

explanation.surface: Nibbling at food a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Done gradually, in small stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Won over church with weapons

parts.note: carrying weapons is being armed

explanation.surface: A militant church persuading people by force of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone won over has been delighted or captivated.

clue.text: Key chaps in charge over picture house

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the pieces are turned upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: A is a musical key
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Key staff in charge of a picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns A + MEN + IC, giving AMENIC backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture house is an old-fashioned term for a film theatre.

clue.text: A southern hard wood

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A hardwood from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree whose timber is a common wood.

clue.text: Short man plunges into water in tropical isles

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for a man is cut off

parts.note: a man is a male
plunging into water is diving, so dives

explanation.surface: A short man diving into the sea at a tropical resort.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation of coral atolls in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Explode one day outside public school

indicators.note: the word for one day goes around the school, with the school inside it

parts.note: a date is one particular day
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A bomb going off one day near a public school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a fee-paying private school; Eton is the most famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb or blow up.

clue.text: Son harbours desire to be a theatre worker?

indicators.note: harbours means the word son holds something within it

parts.note: taken as written
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A son secretly wishing to work in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who operates works in an operating theatre; the question mark flags the misleading sense.

clue.text: Composer's unfortunate sloth

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the letters of sloth have been knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: A composer cursed with idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets.

clue.text: Leave for each embassy

parts.note: per means for each
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: Time off granted to each embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave in the sense of permission given, as in by your leave.

clue.text: Position on board is grounds for divorce?

definitions.meaning: a chess position in which no legal move is possible
read as ..., a spouse who has grown dull

explanation.definitionFit: In chess it is a drawn deadlock; split into two words it is a tired partner.

clue.text: Doctor admitting cause of death

parts.note: admitting something is owning up to it

explanation.surface: A doctor conceding what killed a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocation in water is a common way to die.

clue.text: Severely criticise the working group of famous people

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A critic savaging a working group of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a set of revered or illustrious figures, as in a temple to the gods.

clue.text: Newspaper customer is university lecturer

definitions.meaning: someone who buys and reads a paper
a senior academic rank in British universities, just below professor

explanation.surface: An academic who also buys the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reads the paper; in British universities also a senior teaching post.

clue.text: Bemoan lieutenant having the last word inside

indicators.note: inside means the last word sits within the abbreviation for lieutenant

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer

explanation.surface: A lieutenant moaning because someone else always has the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' is the word that closes a prayer, not having the final say in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn or grieve over something aloud.

clue.text: Perhaps getting cold and disdainful

definitions.meaning: sniffling, as someone coming down with a cold might be

explanation.definitionFit: Literally runny-nosed with a cold; informally, contemptuous and sneering.

clue.text: Spoiler of fun is clear in unfortunate tweet

indicators.note: in means the word for clear goes within the jumbled letters
an unfortunate tweet is a garbled one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a clear page is blank

explanation.surface: A killjoy's ill-judged social media post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' makes WETET from 'tweet'; 'in' puts BLANK after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a person who dampens others' enjoyment.

clue.text: No time in Hertfordshire town to call

indicators.note: no means the time letter is to be absent from the town's name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, England

explanation.surface: No time to phone while in a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To phone someone, as in give me a ring.

clue.text: Opening race perhaps fails to start

indicators.note: fails to start means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: a race is an example of a sporting event

explanation.surface: A race that never gets going at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture or outlet letting air or gas through.

clue.text: Island with wood is perfect

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A wooded island is paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that could not be better.

clue.text: Clown at heart is depressed

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of the word clown

explanation.surface: The sad clown, gloomy underneath the greasepaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down or dejected.

clue.text: Delicate scrap of fabric placed in folder

indicators.note: placed in means the scrap goes inside the folder word

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A fragile fabric swatch slipped into a document folder.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily broken or damaged.

clue.text: Criminal group with course of action on which to embark

parts.note: a gang is a group of criminals
a way is a method or course of action

explanation.surface: A gang plotting a crime they intend to launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on which to embark' reads as a plan to undertake, but it is the walkway for boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A movable bridge used for boarding a ship.

clue.text: A number of heavy objects uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: weights are heavy objects

explanation.surface: Several heavy objects revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' removes W and S from WEIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal numeral, one more than seven.
